purpose: The service-level reuse decision record. It exists so that no Creative use case calls a legacy advertising service by accident, and so that the four services which genuinely are shared are reused instead of rebuilt.

summary.classification: RECOMMENDATION derived from the rows below
summary.headline: Of 48 services, 6 are reusable by Creative (directly or through a contract) and 10 are pattern-only. The remaining 32 must not be called from Creative code. Only 1 of the 48 takes a real row lock (InventoryService), and it locks advertising inventory, so Creative inherits no lock discipline from a service - it must be designed per aggregate.

verified_totals.measurement_note: Comment-stripped counts: docblocks and inline comments are removed before counting, so these are real call expressions. 14 of 48 services contain a real DB::transaction( call; only 1 service (InventoryService) contains a real ->lockForUpdate( call. CommissionService.php mentions lockForUpdate only in a docblock (line 19): its lock was relocated to app/Infrastructure/Financial/Persistence/EloquentPartnerCommissionRepository.php:31 in Phase 0.10. Across app/ as a whole there are 3 real lock call sites (InventoryService.php:48, EloquentPartnerCommissionRepository.php:31, app/Console/Commands/ExpirePendingBookings.php:56) in 24 files that contain a real DB::transaction( call at 41 sites. An earlier figure of 26 transaction files / 15 services was a raw string grep that included comment-only matches.

must_not_be_called_from_creative_domain_.statement: Domain and application Creative code must not call these. Each entry states the reason. Artifact 23 is the enforcement companion; artifact 22 rule D is the boundary statement.

groups.group: Every service that imports App\Models (41 of 48)
groups.reason: A service that reaches for Eloquent models is a persistence-bound application service, not a domain collaborator. Calling it from Creative domain logic drags Active Record into the domain and defeats the boundary ArchitectureRuleTest enforces.
groups.how_to_check: grep the App\Models import list in the dependencies block of each row above.

groups.group: Advertising financial services (PaymentService, RefundService, SettlementService, CommissionService, RevenueDistributionService, RevenueSplitResolverService, FinanceService, FirstBookingDiscountService)
groups.reason: Their rules, columns and state machines are advertising- and provider-specific. Creative reuses PaymentGatewayInterface, not PaymentService. Any Creative financial use case is new.
groups.how_to_check: financial regression suites in AGENTS.md section 10 must not change behaviour.

groups.group: Booking and inventory services (ManualBookingService, BookingCapacityService, ConflictDetectionService, InventoryService, BookingWorkflowService, BookingPriceCalculator)
groups.reason: Protected booking and availability behaviour (AGENTS.md section 11). Creative must not create a campaign booking, and must not introduce creative work into the booking aggregate.

groups.group: Pricing services (PricingService, PricingEngine, PricingRuleEngine, CampaignPricingService, Pricing/* calculators)
groups.reason: They price advertising media time and several operate on float totals. Creative quote derivation is a small deterministic Creative calculation, frozen at acceptance.

groups.group: Analytics and reporting services (ReportService, ProfileService, FinanceService, *AnalyticsService)
groups.reason: They are read services over advertising records. Creative reporting reads Creative records and must never recalculate a Creative amount.
groups.how_to_check: A Creative report that calls these is reading advertising economics, not Creative economics.

groups.group: Discovery and inventory services (BudgetRecommendationService, AssetService, AssetImportService, ScreenDeletionService, Campaign/ClientService, Campaign/AssetDiscoveryFilterService, Campaign/RecommendationService, Campaign/CoverageService)
groups.reason: They operate on advertising inventory, whose meaning ('Asset' = purchasable ad slot) collides confusingly with Creative vocabulary.
groups.how_to_check: Name collision list in artifact 21 ownership conflicts.

groups.group: Partner and loyalty services (PartnerService, Campaign/ReferralService, Campaign/ReferralTrackingService, Campaign/LoyaltyService)
groups.reason: A creator is not an affiliate partner, and loyalty points are not money.
groups.how_to_check: partner_commissions and reward_* must be untouched by Creative.

creative_relevant_services_absent.statement: None of the following exists anywhere in app/ as of 2026-09-26: a Creative application service, a Creative domain service, a Creative repository, a Creative use-case handler, a Creative event, a Creative Mailable, a Creative policy, a Creative job, or a Creative query class.
creative_relevant_services_absent.evidence: app/Domain/Creative, app/Services/Creative, app/Repositories/Creative, app/Http/Controllers/Creative, app/Http/Requests/Creative, app/Http/Resources/Creative and app/Policies do not exist; find app -type d -empty returns nothing.
creative_relevant_services_absent.consequence: The entire Creative application and domain layer is NEW work. Artifacts 20 and 24 define it. The only Creative-compatible services that exist are the five shared services listed above.
